DONE (s470bq, Opus, 2026-09-05).  Grammar, both reader sketches (Perl and
JavaScript) and the declared boundary are docs/ir-spec.md Â§12b;
docs/generated-cl-ir-review.md Â§3.1 item 7 updated with how its warning was
answered.

`Pl/DataForm.pm` prints the lowered tree so a consumer never implements CL's
five reader rules (Â§11b): every symbol pipe-quoted (a keyword's colon INSIDE
the bars, a package qualifier inside them too), strings 7-bit with exactly six
escapes and surrogate pairs above the BMP, numbers decimal (a `#x41` radix
literal converted), a quoted symbol `(|quote| |X|)` and a character
`(|char| N)`, one top-level form per line, no comments.  `(p-esc â¦)` collapses
to the plain string it denotes -- the data form has its own escapes.

ORDER IS THE PROGRAM: the collector buffers by (section, bucket) and replays
in the assembly's phase order -- every section's compile buckets, then every
section's run bucket (#469's phase model).  `Pl::Passes::run` forwards the
BUCKET to the observer hook and Parser2's four call sites label it;
`(|p-bucket| SECTION |:BUCKET| |:PHASE|)` marks each run.

THE REVIEW DOC WARNED "do not build this before the seams are gone; a sexp
dump with embedded text islands is worse than no dump."  The answer is that
every island is DECLARED and COUNTED: `(|p-cl-text| "â¦")` for a Raw leaf or a
pre-spelled CL atom, `(|p-cl-text-wrap| "â¦" CLOSERS formâ¦)` for a raw_wrap,
and `(|p-data-form-end| FORMS ISLANDS)` as the file's last line.  A dump that
says how much of the program it could not structure is not worse than no dump.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT CARRY, stated in Â§12b rather than hidden: the file's
environment preamble and the CL-reader bookkeeping the ASSEMBLY writes as text
(`in-package`, `p-defpackage`, `defclass`, the `$a`/`$b` defvars, the
forward-global defvars, `p-run-compile-phase-blocks`,
`p-set-current-package`).  Those are not lowered forms; expressing them as
trees is the remaining work (task #1217).

THE ~50-LINE CLAIM IS A GATE ROW: Pl/t/ir-data-form-01.t implements that
reader in plain Perl, parses the emission of a fixture carrying every shape,
and RE-PRINTS byte-identically.
